subject: ventures/brrrr-calculator
professional: a BRRRR investor-lender: a loan officer who writes DSCR and cash-out refinances for rehab investors and underwrites hard-money exits. First checks: is the refinance sized on appraisal or cost basis (seasoning), is the DSCR the lender's rent/PITIA ratio, and do the hard-money carrying costs and closing costs net out correctly in cash left in the deal.

evidence.correctness: Recomputed the sample deal in an independent Python script (/tmp/claude-0/brrrr/indep.py) from the standard annuity formula and the lender DSCR definition (gross rent / PITIA): all-in 209,762.50, cash in 42,262.50, DSCR-supported loan 233,090.60, refinance 187,500 (LTV binds), cash left 26,950, P&I 1,247.44/mo, NOI 16,288.40, cash flow 1,319.09, all equal to the tool (node /tmp/claude-0/brrrr/tool.mjs). Max price for zero cash left solved in closed form (hard-money loan cancels: cash left = all-in - refi x (1 - refi closing)) = 125,360.00 vs bisection 125,360.46 (0.5 tolerance). 70% rule 135,000. DSCR-capped loan at rent 1,200 / DSCR 1.25 = 90,435.05 both ways. Payment check 200k/6%/30y = 1,199.10 matches standard amortization tables. Engine is right; held at 3 not 4 because the page let blank fields silently become zero while showing non-zero example placeholders (defect 0).
evidence.completeness: Every README/page feature works end to end in the engine: cash in, cash out, cash left, cash flow, NOI DSCR, DSCR-capped refinance with limitedBy, max price, 70% comparison, ARV/overrun/rate stress tables, CSV with formula neutralising, usage opt-out. No TODOs or stubs. dscrRent is computed but never shown.
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs': 28/28 pass before the fix (30/30 after). Hand-computed costs are asserted to the cent. Seeded 4 mutants via quality_mutate.py: refinance closing costs on the LTV loan instead of the capped loan SURVIVED; HOA dropped from the DSCR cap SURVIVED; management/maintenance on gross instead of EGI caught; bisection tolerance 0.5 -> 50 caught. Half the seeded mutants in the DSCR-cap path survived, so 2.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (157 lines), index.html, page.test.mjs, usage.mjs. Small, pure, deterministic engine; numeric parsing strict (rejects 1e5, accepts $1,250); output escaped; CSV formula injection guarded; storage access wrapped. Defects: the placeholder/default mismatch (input handling), unused dscrRent, a misleading comment on allInPctArv (calc.mjs:64), hard-money cap check at calc.mjs:101 is unreachable (range already 0-100).
evidence.claims: README model section matches calc.mjs line by line (hard loan, all-in, cash in, refi cap, cash out, cash left floor, bisection). 'Nothing is uploaded' backed by page.test.mjs (no fetch/XHR/beacon). Usage events named match index.html record() calls. Not-modelled list and 'Unverified: hand calculation and unit tests only' are honest. Disclaimer present on page and README. llms.txt github.io link is rewritten at deploy (served-copy.mjs: no retired origin left).
evidence.fitness: Walked the job: an investor deciding whether a deal recycles capital. With the example loaded the answer is right and the stress tables are useful. But typing only price, ARV and rent (the status line asks for exactly that) produced NOI 22,743 with zero tax, insurance and management while the inputs displayed 2,800 / 1,500 / 8% as placeholders, and DSCR cap off while 1.1 was shown. And the refinance is always on full ARV at a 6-month default hold, where many lenders cap at cost basis or require seasoning: the very first question a lender asks.
evidence.domain: Matches the standard BRRRR worksheet (cash in = all-in less hard-money; cash out = refi less payoff and closing). DSCR cap uses gross rent over PITIA(+HOA), which is how DSCR lenders size; 75% LTV default matches the common investor cash-out maximum for a 1-unit property; 70% rule is the textbook MAO. Departures, all disclosed in 'Not modelled': seasoning / cost-basis caps on early refinances, hard-money interest on undrawn rehab funds (conservative), no hard-money ARV cap.

defects.what: Optional inputs showed example placeholders (property tax 2800, insurance 1500, management 8%, maintenance 6%, min DSCR 1.1, carry 450, hard-money 85%/100%, rehab 40000) while a blank field counted as 0 (maintenance 5): a user who typed only price, ARV and rent, as the status line asks, got NOI and cash flow overstated by about $6,455/yr on the sample (NOI 22,743 vs 16,288) and the DSCR cap silently off.

Two of four seeded mutants in the DSCR-cap path survived: refinance closing costs charged on the LTV loan instead of the capped loan, and HOA dropped from the DSCR loan cap (tests only use hoa 0 and the capped case never checks refi costs).

The refinance is always sized on ARV. Early refinances (the 6-month default hold) are commonly capped at cost basis or need title seasoning before a cash-out; disclosed only in the Not-modelled list, so the headline cash-left number is the optimistic case.

Tile and rate table show NOI-based DSCR (1.09 on the sample, below the 1.1 minimum entered) while the lender cap uses rent/PITIA (1.31); the rent-based dscrRent is computed but never shown, which reads as a contradiction.
Hard-money interest charged on the full rehab amount for the whole hold (draws are funded in arrears), and no hard-money cap on ARV or total cost: conservative, unflagged on the page.
Comment on allInPctArv says 'total cash-in plus the drag of the refinance costs' but the value is all-in cost / ARV; the >100 hard-money check is unreachable after range validation.

verdict: The BRRRR engine is arithmetically right: six outputs recomputed independently (annuity formula, rent/PITIA DSCR, closed-form max price, 70% rule) match to the cent. Claims are backed and limits honestly stated. It misses the bar on verification: half the seeded mutants in the DSCR-cap path survived. The worst defect was on the page: optional fields showed realistic example placeholders while blank meant zero, so the minimal input the page asks for overstated cash flow and turned the DSCR cap off. Fixed in this session (placeholders now show the blank value, a note explains it, and a test ties each placeholder to the engine's default); tests added for both surviving mutants. A lender would still first ask about seasoning and cost-basis caps, which are disclosed but not modelled.
